Dawn of Origin 5 is a dual Moog song. 
The left side was recorded live first
and the right side was played live over top.
The song was created for Gorgolon, a story of 
an underwater civilization in 1994.

Origin 5 was the fifth AI direction 
to save a planet as water levels increased.
They were to form bubbles from glass made 
where ocean sands met molten core 
and blown with chrome tubes.

Gorgolonians live in the bubbles. 
They heat air at the base which rises 
and sucks air down from the surface.
They fly red chrome saucers through the tubes 
and report findings to Origin 5.

The story was made into a Dan Zen multi-user Web game 
in 1996 to spot the artificial intelligence.

Signals for Origin 5 captures the communication 
between the two Moogs with an exciting visualization.
The original song has been broken into 5 movements:
Contact, Agreement, Transfer, Discussion, Farewell.

15019.d:
'Hashway 69 Revisited' by pixelwank
Following on from BlockonBlock, this is the evolution of that concept. 

Whether you're a Dylan or a Degen, the Hashies are for everyone. 

These give me feelings of warmth and hope or isolation & loneliness - depending on the output or my headspace at the time of viewing. 

These include a bunch of variables including:
- 23 colour palettes 
- 'dusk' or 'day' colour overlays 
- roads (%80), train tracks(15%) or paths(5%)
- clouds
- windows on the buildings & number of buildings 
- mountains 
- grasses & pond 
- moon/sun & sky texture 
& more... 

Click the image or press 's' or 'S' in live move for a 3000x3000 png 
Can look into doing even more hi-res copies for collectors in the future (I think!)

Also apologies for long loading time, my coding will get better! hehe 

This is somewhat of a culmination of the last few months learning and digging into p5js & generative art and I'm super proud of these. Thanks for collecting.
Big shoutout to all the frens at Circolors for the love and support. 
Also big shoutout to the FxHash community for being so welcoming & supportive.

R.I.F.F.
Remember It's For Fun

15027.d:
'Get Out of My Head' is the first generative micro-blockbuster on fx(hash)! Mystery, suspense, a spectacular finale and many of the best parts of the coolest celebrities combined by an algorithm into a single artwork.

----------------------------
* Just click to play/pause the movie.
* Press [v] to on/off sound.
----------------------------

SUMMARY OF PREVIOUS EPISODES

By the beginning of the census campaign, it was not possible to meet Brity with a clear look - a black patch replaced at least one eye of each individual. Their thoughts, behavior, reasoning, attitude towards others, towards themselves, towards life — all this became dark in an instant! But Mr. Lived declared victory early. A small group of brave Brities opened up resistance, trying to beat this damn crap out of themselves!


PROJECT DETAILS

'Get Out of My Head' generative animated collection in its art component is the search for new solutions, transfer to the cinema territory and the development of the classic absurdist Dada collage; from a technical point of view, this project is an exploration of the p5.js' multimedia capabilities.

Coding the Animation
The animation prototype was made in After Effects, then the coordinates and angle of rotation changes for each element were exported to a data file. When playing a movie, the algorithm reads this data frame by frame and animates the scene.

Elements Library
The audiovisual library, from which the algorithm selects parts for the assembly of each movie, contains over 400 elements: 92 celebrity eyes, 63 noses, 78 mouths, 66 hairstyles, 5 body types (hereinafter within each type there are several options for elements), 12 bikini types, 7 weapon types, 9 badge types, 4 necklace types, 5 sound types and 4 different bangs.

Star Cast
See Features to find out which parts of which cool celebrities are featured in your movie!

Created and directed by @m5alien

15031.d:
Robo Ishiguro is a tribute to the writing of Kazuo Ishiguro. It is a poor attempt to capture the beauty of Ishiguro's estranged and slightly skewed writing that leaves you living in an incomplete memory. This work is especially inspired by Ishiguro's story 'A village after dark'.
 
The prose is a slotted generative work, each piece written by me, then chosen and arranged by the algorithm. The background is a looped animation that should mimic: a fog, a rain, the autumn. The text is placed on a unique tablet shape. The work is best viewed at 1:1 or portrait. I've thought of it as the back blurb of a novel or the readout in a silent film.

 
Just javascript.
Made by DSims (dillansimmons.com)
https://objkt.com/profile/tz1Q4YfANpgKAuPXd1fobzBzdjg6wtPmmw5m

- 's': Export the SVG document describing the arrangement of hatch lines.

15045.d:
Organic Illusion is one of the very first computer graphic drawings I produced that I considered worthy of being called Art. This version is a Plotter Art reconstruction of one of my classics.

Between 1973 - 1975 I was working on an MFA in Graphic Design at Michigan State University. I was using the most rudimentary hardware and software. All graphics were produced by writing code in FORTRAN, punching each line of code into a Hollerith card, assembling cards into a deck and submitting the deck for processing on a main frame at a central computing facility. You returned the next day to pick up your plot which was processed over night on an off-line plotter. I exhibited this piece in my MFA show in 1975.

Back then the only "graphic primitive" we had available to create a drawing was the command to move a pen and draw a line: CALL PLOT(X, Y, penUp) and CALL PLOT(X, Y, penDown). Organic Illusion is an early example of an algorithmic image (non representational/non digitized) employing controlled randomness. It is a regular grid of square tiles that connect. Each tile consists of a square with its perimeter divided into the same number of points as the circle it contains. Randomness determines the placement of the circles’ center relative to the center of the square. The way the coordinate points between the two shapes are connected appear to create a volume, i.e. 3D illusion. 

The code for the original image is long gone but I was able to reconstruct it from memory. Like a child you never forget. I submit to you again in new media for you all to enjoy.

Check out Dr. Bill Generative Art OG website @ drbillkolomyjec.com

“Shapes on a Plane” explores imaginary structures and worlds through simple shapes. It’s intended for small-scale print.

As a kid I was obsessed with Lego, Duplo, wooden building blocks... anything I could make something with.

I’d spend hours building things, imagining new worlds, new machines, new concepts, then i’d take them apart and create a whole new idea to explore.

To me, this piece to me is a reminder of that time - many days spent exploring ideas with those simple objects - no care for viability, for marketability, for audiences or business. Just pure fun.

Without this time in my life, I doubt I’d have found my passion for creating in the way I do today.

A forest has stories to tell.
About times that were, about times that will be.
-
This project was minted in much unusual conditions. 
We gathered here, by 38 degrees heat. We belong to a crowd who loves stories, of civilisations at stake and deities, of afterlife and worship. We drank and hugged and chanted pagan hymns. We minted the Bugged Forest from our place on earth that we call Hell just for the fun of it. We are passionate, and loving, and angry and desperate. We, people of the soil, under a bugged sun.
-
This project is the long-form version of an algorithm that contains a bug. “The Bugged Tree”’s code was salvaged and stored and served as the core motivation and engine for an entire forest. Its concept is about releasing the control. I am a  byproduct of evolution, an iteration of that specie who wanted utter control, and which at some point, lost control over its own creation. As a generative artist, I chose to welcome the event of chance into my creative process. The symbolism in chance made me feel humble and free. Unwilling to make any change to a story that the Tree needed to tell me, as a listener, rather than a writer of my own idealised fantasies.
-
The iterations aren’t under control. They may be odd and off. We have to accept it. They are also plottable, press [s] in live mode to get a SVG. Attempt the plot at your own risk, as there’s a possibility for it to come near to impossibilities or cause paper or motor damage, and most certainly, a bugged drawing.
-
From Earth or from Hell, with love, yours truthfully, NFTBiker and zancan

‘Imperfect Images of Transuranic Metals’

Transuranic elements occupy that thin, narrow part of the periodic table that is snipped out of the main body and rendered beneath it. They are fleeting, transient elements, their existences dependent upon artifice and manipulation. Particle accelerators force particles into unnatural configurations; nuclear explosions tear apart the fabric of atoms, or the inhospitable environment of a reactor provides fertile ground to birth these unstable and dangerous materials.

‘Imperfect Images of Transuranic Metals’ continues the themes begun in ‘The Last Days of Fire and Steel’ and ‘Mapped Orbits for Unbound Electrons’; the continuation of a minor obsession with the darker side of particle physics.

Generation

Beyond the story, the process by which the piece is generated is a subtle dance of chaos and probability. Three variables control the structure of each molecule, which is generated in a 3D space.

The molecules are fashioned from a grid arrangement, extending in varying fashions along the x-, y- and z-axis. Each segment of the molecule varies in size, and has the possibility of being rendered as a sphere, cube or cone. Probabilities are manipulated to group these possibilities, actively forming the shape of the molecule and avoiding a mere random cloud.

After its creation, the molecule is flattened down to two dimensions at a chosen angle, and shading and drop-shadows are added to simulate a reflective metal surface. Some colour is added, but the piece is generally close to monochrome.

The whole render takes place in p5js, with no external libraries or shaders.

In the next step, all of the extracted characters will be produced and released in full shot view and in different modes of life processes and occupations.

Closing remarks:
Because I had the opportunity and motivation to produce a small portion of future PFP characters, I need to appreciate people who supported me. 
Special thanks to the management team of fx(hash), women In gen-art and all the dear collectors.

15093.d:
Sing_2022, by Stephen Boyd  
June, 2022  
Little India, Toronto, Canada.

** Sing_2022 will begin animating 4 seconds after loading.
** It can take up to 5 seconds to load depending on features.


Project Description
---
Sing_2022 is a re-imagining of a series of prints I created in 2004 called "Sing Red" and "Sing Neon". See the included ./documentation/ folder for images.

The concept from the original Sing series is as follows:
> Read each row of pixels in a source image and then redraw those pixels across the middle of a canvas in the shape of a sin curve while altering the amplitude and period based on the characteristics of the colours in each row.

Sing_2022's underlying concept is very similar to the 2004 original but with some key additions. The biggest changes are the inclusion of animation and multiple layers of sin curves.

The variables that are determined at the time of minting include:
- the image chosen as the substrate, which is selected from seven potential images,
- the number of layers of curves (two or three layers)
- the resolution of each layer, meaning the height of each strip to be redrawn, and,
- a theta offset value that influences the initial arrangement of each layer's curves

The image at animation frame 0 is the intended static representation of the work. However, it can be exported at any point to a PNG file (and at multiple resolutions without losing consistency).


Interaction
---
Animation Control
Sing_2022 will remain still for 4 seconds before beginning to animate.
- Press 'z' before animation starts to hold at frame 0.
- Press 'a' to toggle the animation on and off.

Export to PNG
Export to a PNG format at several different sizes.
- Press t: thumbnail @ 200x200
- Press s: your current screen size
- Press p: print size @ 4800x4800 which is 16"@300dpi
- Press h: HD4K on the vertical @ 2160x2160
- Press m: Max size @ 10800x10800 This is a biiiig size

I've added code that will re-render the iteration at each of the sizes listed below while retaining its exact characteristics. This is considerably better than trying to up or downscale an image.

The filename will include some metadata such as the unique hash, date and time of export and the animation frame at time of capture.

15109.d:
This work is inspired by thinking about lines. Points, lines, and surfaces are the most basic elements of art. Whether or not an art work can be made using only lines and colors is a direction that has been explored recently. By connecting points at different distances, the color and transparency can produce different light and shade effects with the change of distance. In addition, a rotation algorithm is generated during the connection process, which can create light and shade, density, and the beauty of curves with relatively rich layers. , like a swallow dancing in the air is the resulting arc path. Hence the name Yanwu. Of course, another Chinese meaning of Yanwu is a brand of early Chinese TV sets, which also commemorates the era of creativity. I am also grateful to be able to contribute to the construction of Web3. There are 3 background colors, 7 line colors, and 30 dance times in this work, among which there are millions of combinations of point positions. This work only displays the background color, line color and dance times in the feature information.
Made With P5.js.
20% of royalties will be donated to the Processing Foundation.

An experiment with walkers and particles. The sketch starts by creating lines according to the path taken by the walkers (8 possible directions), then particles are emitted along these lines. The program has two possibilities, two modes to diffuse the particles, flame and splash, they determine how the particles will be affected by a Perlin noise.

The One Tezo Drawings project is a variation of the “Desenhos de um Real” project (2006- ). In it, the artist sets the price of his work by making a rational calculation, equating his artistic production with a consumer good detached from the art world .
In this case, the calculation is based on the amount charged per hour of work from the minimum wage in the United States. Thus, a drawing that took X hours to produce (Wt) will have its price fixed at USD 15.00 * Wt divided by the value in Dollars of one Tezo (Dt) at the time of publication. But for the final price to be 1.00 Tez, the total production time value (Wt) will be divided by the number of editions (Ed). Therefore, the number of editions is defined by the following formula: 1.00 Tez = (Wt*15/Dt)/Ed ==> 

Ed=Wt*15/Dt 

For this particular project:
Permutation of 5 almost mirrored layers of drawings of bodies

Wt= 3,5
Dt= 1,31
Ed= 4,5*15/1.31 = 40

Press J or P to save a 1500x1500px image

15125.d:
ðolmen is a generative art project by Diego Pintos.
It draws rectangles with points instead a plain color or border. With some variations in the distribution of this points, we get a kind of noise depth effect.

12 carefully selected palettes. Based in Art Masterpieces and in Nature.
· Gioconda (Leonardo da Vinci)
· Guernika (Pablo Picasso)
· Nighthawks (Edward Hopper)
· Meninas (Diego Velazquez)
· Judith beheading Holofernes (Caravaggio)
· Al Siq (nature)
· guacamayo (nature)
· Salamanca (nature)
· mostaza (nature)
· Timanfaya (nature)
· piedra (nature)
· firefall (nature)

ðolmen builds 10 compositions:
· Square
· PersonChen's Style
· Equilibrium
· Hanging
· Pyramid
· Row
· Column
· 3 columns (randomly aligned)
· 3 rows (randomly aligned)
· Frame

Density
· Tiny: Less than 35 rects. Rare
· Small: Less than 100 rects. Common.
· Medium: Less than 250 rects. Common.
· High: Less than 350 rects. Common.
· Massive: Less than 500 rects. Rare.
· Ultra: More than 500 rects. Rarest.

Rarities
· Rectangle filling type: Filled (95%) or unfilled (5%)
· Monochrome: Just black and white. Always unfilled. (1%)
· Dark mode: Dark background (20%). Dark mode can be monochrome.
· Habitable (90%). See humans later.

Humans
ðolmen can host tiny humans. Contains a little code that draws humans looking down, in order to to provide size perspective.

Minting
Each ðolmen contains all rarities inside. As a ðolmen collector, you can display your final piece in all available formats, and rarity owners can display the regular filled composition. In addition, this can help if you want to print one or more formats.

Tricks and Keys
ðolmen is responsive, you can zoom out your browser window and refresh to get a larger output.
's' save the current canvas
'd' toggle dark mode
'f' toggle fill mode
'm' toggle monochrome

More info and visual description:
https://thelirios.com/dolmen/

Based on ideas taken from a mathematical model for analyzing how collisions between gravity fields in deep space work, used to chronicle the complex interactions between colliding singularities, modelling the collapse therein. It also has relation to the simple rules underlying flocking behaviour in birds, but without interaction between individuals within the flock.

There's also the issue that once, Michael Jackson had to hold onto a fan to prevent him plummeting to his doom from a crane. I think the poor deluded soul thought Michael was hugging him, as he chose to raise his arms and rock gently in the arms of the King of Pop, a vague smile on his face.

The climate is also changing: a gentle meditation can bring peace to a changing world, and allow us all to take stock of where we are and where we are heading.

The hue range in this is variable, and the complexity and zoom are also based on the intial values provided by fxhash.

I hope you like it, and stay away from cranes, particularly with that carbon footprint.

Multiverse - EnergyMerge
Do you believe Multiverse ( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiverse)?
Can you feel the mysterious force of dark energy exploded, exchanged, and merged in the field, which happened with every second in the universes.
How about the high dimensions of our universe? Can you imagine objects with dimensions greater than 3?

Two big energy regions (a black hole and a white hole) are twisting the gravity field of the universe. Raging energy is moving in the field.

With a low probability, a single energy region occurs and forms an energy field with an unary singularity.

Please be patient with drawing process :)

An exploration on the ways in which mental energy might be captured and converted to kinetic destruction.

Each piece begins with an abstract shape. The shape is subjected to a field of disruptors, which contains a combination of beams and bombs. Beams slice through material, shearing fragments generally in the direction the beam is traveling. Bombs shatter material apart and eject shards away from the blast site.

All matter is conserved. That is, if the exploded and scattered fragments were reverted back to their initial positions, there would be a fully intact shape. No virtual particles. 🖤

Some structures may be annihilated. Others may take minor damage — or perhaps, none at all. Consult the “telekinetic power” feature for a full assessment.

Some artists combine these two concepts to create unsettling tessellation glitches. By creating tessellations out of digital images that contain glitches, they are able to create images that are both visually interesting and subtly disturbing.

City. Perhaps It is the best work of art that humans and nature create together. Inspired by numerous city landscape photos, "The Color of Cities" series abstracts the city's repeating days. 

Each city in the work repeats a day with different weather, color and detailed compositions. A day is divided into three sessions (Morning/Sunset/Night), each lasting for 20 seconds.
A day here is equivalent to one minute in our real world. After one minute passes, another day begins with the same settings.

- Weather: Clear / Snow(I/II) / Rain(I/II) 
- Morning: 6 color palettes 
- Sunset: 12 color palettes 
- Night: 8 color palettes 
- Street light types: White / Orange 
- Special night event: None / Fireworks / SkyLanterns
- Moon: 9 modes 
- Sun: 3 modes 
- Meteors: 4 levels 
- Stars: 4 levels 
- Vehicles: 4 levels 
- Buildings: 2 modes 

[d] toggle detail info
[s] capture and download snapshot 
[left click on the sky] add stars (temporarily) 

Enjoy this small world!

15218.d:
There’s so much more to our world than what we are able to perceive, let alone understand. Will we ever be able to even fully understand ourselves?

–

Elevation is a series of 320 generative elevation drawings of imaginary structures. It is a reminder of the limits of our consciousness, and an ode to the manifold nuances that lie beyond what we can perceive, beyond what we even can imagine.

As a generative artist, I aim to elevate my own consciousness with the help of the machine. I welcome algorithms and randomness into the creation of my works, taking full control, and intentionally giving it away, always seeking to expand my imagination. For as humans alone, we remain limited to our own edifice of thought, and often fail to free ourselves from the visible, mundane world.

Both are present in Elevation: the visible and the imaginary, the mundane and the transcendent, the solid and the fragile. Where an architect’s elevation drawing marks the transition from the thought world into the visible world, Elevation remains in-between, depicting both the idea of an imaginary structure, and the structure itself.

–

Elevation is intended for print. All holders of an Elevation NFT will be able to order the corresponding signed print in the respective paper format via andreasrau.eu/elevation. Press [s] to save the image as displayed or [p] to generate a print-ready PNG image at 300 dpi. This might take a while, depending on paper format and your hardware.

–

Elevation
p5.js, glsl, html, css
Andreas Rau, 2022

Sketch is an open-ended series. Works evolve as I code a generative project, sometimes drastically. Intermediate works usually don't see the light of day - they get archived and forgotten. This series is snapshots of different forms along the way - each standing alone, but also part of a larger meandering work flow. The word Sketch implies incompleteness. 15224.d:
Vanilla javascript and some css on SVG from bitmap input.

Owners of previous version will receive a free update.

The most interesting aspect of this work is the use of some public domain artwork bitmap images as input dataset to generate a randomized grid of blended triangular surfaces.

Triangle is the basic shape from which it's possible to construct all other shapes, at least on a finite discrete grid like our screens. How not to adore triangles blessing our screen?

The goal of this work is not trying to catch the "essential", the "vibe", or the "atmosphere" from an input artwork, neither to parasite it and shine with it's reflected light. The input images are a way to random noise, but you can use your own and you'll see that Triagulatria's own character will be preserved and you'll have even more good time.

For this new version I changed the image composition technique due to browsers svg painting delay issues when the number of triangles is big. Now triangles are rendered one by one and drawn onto a canvas element to get the final image performing a delightful animation.

Why"serendipity"?
The changes I made to Triangulatria have an interesting "feedback" side effect that will be removed on the next version, but that I also would like to keep track of it.  

Note: I tuned and selected different configurations of Triangulatria. Some of them in some cases may produce just a black square. It's a valid artistic outcome but I will reserve some mints to exchange them with the black ones, at my sole discretion (ask me for the change if you want it)

Inertial Packing 001 ('IP.001') is the first in a new 'Studies' series exploring technical aspects of larger projects.

IP.001 includes multiple constraint systems, based on Verlet and Euler Integration approaches. Numerous user controls are included:

Interaction:

Mouse/Trackpad:
drag -> camera rotation
drag + CMD/CTR -> camera pan
scroll wheel/pinch -> camera zoom

Key Input:
-, +: reduce | increase  Node Count
{, }: reduce | increase  Packing Dimension
c, v: reduce | increase  Node Adhesion
h, j: reduce | increase  Node Jitter
b, n: disable| enable    Node-Node Collision
z, x: reduce | increase  Stick Constraint
a, s: hide   | show      Nodes
q, w: hide   | show      Wireframe
p: screen capture

Tip:
1. There are 8 unique geometries, should you be inclined to collect a full set.
2. Bringing values outside of "rational" range is encouraged.

Note:
Please post your favorite IP.001 screen captures
TW: @iragreenberg
IG: @greenberg.ira

Built with Three.js, PByte.js, TypeScript, Node

15232.d:
Some arbitrary geometric shapes that hover in place until interacted with.

Each click will animate each shape to a new randomised position (x, y, z), as well as play some hits from a selection of random scales.

The longer you hold your pointer down, the more tension builds, resulting in a more intense shape displacement as well as a faster playing speed on the tones.

Doing that for long enough will also trigger one out of two effects, either putting a sepia layer over the scene or encapsulating it with a darkened vignette. There’s about a 3% chance of not getting a “hold-in effect” but instead getting your whole scene rendered with a chromatic aberration.

There are 2 different instruments to collect. A Berlin Concert Grand Piano and a Harmonised 3-Oscillator Pad.

There’s about a 3.2% chance of getting a spheric shape instead of a cubic shape.

In addition to all this, you can get various amounts of shape counts, and each one can have a different color theming as well as different metalness and roughness materials.

There’s also a plethora of different lightings to get such as ambient, point and spotlights in different color themes.

Finally there’s a percentage indicator that reflects the uniqueness of each shape composition down to a finer detail, taking all of these parameters in account.

@computeremotions - 2022-06-19

This work explores the inheritance of design parameters within a single tree lineage. Studied characteristics include length/diameter balance, branching strategy, leaf distribution, orientation, and color details. In addition, the environment provides wind and season information.     
Each new tree is created by replicating the attributes of its immediate ancestor, but subject to a controlled mutation rate.

Finally a photograph is taken with a simple snapshot or, with a long exposure setting capturing branch and leaf movements.

Try resizing the browser window to experiment with different aspect ratios. The system will switch to a single line layout if enough horizontal space is available.

Press "2" To "4" to increase the resolution
Press "S" to download a PNG file.

Built with p5js.
